kashika: अच्च हल् च अज्झलौ। तुल्यास्यप्रयत्नावपि अज्झलौ परस्परं सवर्णसंज्ञौ न भवतः। अवर्णहकारौ — दण्डहस्तः। इवर्णशकारौ — दधि शीतम् । सवर्णदीर्घत्वं न भवति। वैपाशो मत्स्यः। आनडुहं चर्मेति <<यस्येति च>> [[६.४.१४८]] इति लोपो न भवति॥
kashikaEnglish: A vowel and a consonant are never savarṇa of each other.
englishShort: A स्वर and a व्यञ्जन cannot be सवर्ण of each other.
englishFull:
But अ and आ are always सवर्ण with other vowels for purposes of प्रत्याहार (abbreviatory notation).

The particle तु ("but") indicates an exception to @ref[1.1.9].

In pratyāhāras like अच् (all vowels) or अक् (अ इ उ ऋ ऌ), the initial अ stands for all vowels of its class regardless of the strict savarṇa definition.

**Why needed:**
- By @ref[1.1.9], अ (throat, open) and इ (palate, open) differ in place — not savarṇa
- But the Śivasūtra अइउण् must denote all simple vowels
- This rule makes अ/आ "universal representatives" in pratyāhāras

**Result:**
When अ appears in a pratyāhāra, it stands for:
- अ, आ (its true savarṇas)
- इ, ई, उ, ऊ, ऋ, ॠ, ऌ, ॡ (by this exception)

This is limited to pratyāhāras only, not to other grammatical operations.
